conventions.convention: Signature is (-,+,+,+); x⁰=ct and r have length units; r is areal radius; c,G>0 are formal fixed parameters. The source has mixed components diag(-ε,p,p,p), and M=c²r(1-b)/(2G).
The smooth spherical coordinate domain excludes r=0. Center extension is a separate C² Cartesian conclusion obtained from even radial coefficients.
The geometric supplier chain assumes ZF plus Countable Choice, with no full Axiom of Choice asserted.
The entropy chart has s∈C², s_ε>0, Θ=1/s_ε, μ=-Θs_n, and p=Θs+μn-ε. Positive even C² profiles have compact range in the chart and b≥b_*>0. E=c²M(R) is the spherical mass-energy constraint.
Constrained stationarity uses sup-norm C¹ profile curves with smooth compactly supported tangent at zero, fixed R,E,N_b, and lapse normalization φ(R)=½log b(R). It asserts first variation only.
Constant-density regularity requires 0<u<8/9. Interface C¹ regularity is established in the constructed proper-radial matching chart, while the density jumps at R.

load_bearing.statement: Defines g=-e^(2φ)(dx⁰)²+b⁻¹dr²+r²γ, the smooth isotropic mixed source diag(-ε,p,p,p), and M=c²r(1-b)/(2G), without adopting field equations or empirical applicability.
On an open J⊂(0,∞), for smooth φ,b,ε,p with b>0, the full mixed Einstein equations are equivalent to M'=4πr²ε/c², φ'=(GM/c²+4πGr³p/c⁴)/(r²b), and p'=-G(ε+p)(M+4πr³p/c²)/(c²r²b).
For even C² functions f,h on (-δ,δ), f(|x|) and δ_ij+x_ix_jh(|x|) are C² on B_δ(0); consequently b=1-r²q with even C² q and b>0 gives C² Cartesian spatial metric coefficients.

For a smooth positive ε:I_p→(0,∞), compact central-pressure interval P_c with the stated closed margin, and fixed φ_c, there is a common R₀>0 with unique even integral-equation profiles in the pressure ball, smoothness, b≥1/2, a C² Cartesian center, uniform-norm continuous dependence, and compact-interior continuation on r>0.

For ρ₀,R>0 and u=2GM_R/(c²R)∈(0,8/9), the displayed constant-density interior and vacuum exterior solve the equations on their open pieces, have a C² Cartesian center, and join as a C¹ piecewise-C² metric without a delta-supported surface stress. The branch range is necessary and sufficient for the stated regular positive algebraic data.

Under its fixed-radius chart, profile, positive-b and lapse-normalization hypotheses, constrained stationarity is equivalent to constant μ/Θ, Θe^φ and μe^φ; in that case TOV holds, α=μ/Θ and β=1/Θ_K. No maximum, existence or dynamical-stability conclusion is asserted.

concerns.concern: Step 6.1 chooses a closed state ball and then calls it 'convex and open' when invoking the mean-value inequality, whose supplier requires an open convex domain. Apply the inequality on the ball's interior; continuity extends the estimate to its closure if needed. The local-Lipschitz conclusion is unaffected.

The stationarity definition quantifies over arbitrary sup-norm C¹ profile curves, whereas steps 1.1–3.2 explicitly calculate smooth compactly supported directions and finite-parameter affine perturbations. Step 7.1 implicitly extends the first-variation formula to every admissible curve. A short uniform remainder argument would close this: the mass-to-b map is bounded linear in the sup norm, and the state functions and positive-b power have uniformly continuous derivatives on a compact neighborhood, so the functionals are differentiable there and their derivatives depend only on the tangent at zero.
